text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore and Thailand take step forward into new era of closer bilateral ties with agreement to forge enhanced partnership and seek ways to complement each other, not compete.

- Proposed bridge across Straits of Malacca linking peninsular Malaysia to Sumatra in Indonesia will be designed as soon as possible to maximise benefits to both countries, Datuk Seri Dr Mahathir Mohamad says.

- President Suharto orders Coordinating Minister for Welfare Azwar Anas to investigate reports Indonesia has "lost wealth" outside national boundary -- including billions of dollars in bank in Switzerland.

- Minister for Information and Arts George Yeo reiterates his view that Umno Youth chief Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's request to visit Singapore should be interpreted as positive gesture intended to improve bilateral ties.
- Singapore consortium signs Singapore $1 billion joint-venture deal to build industrial park in Thailand, believed to be largest Singapore corporate investment in country.
- Bidders for former U.S. Embassy property at Hill Street have choice of acquiring site either on freehold basis or on 125-year lease.
- Malaysia announces slew of new incentives to boost investment and skills to its international offshore financial centre on Labuan island in South China Sea.
- Deal between Singapore Airlines, Australian carrier Ansett and Air New Zealand expected to be announced as early as this week.
- Initial public offering market holding firm in face of anaemic stock market.
- F&N Coca-Cola, which oversees soft drinks operations of local conglomerate Fraser & Neave Ltd, confident that despite profit dip in first half, it can still expect 1997 profit to double.
- Fraser & Neave property subsidiary, mainboard-listed Centrepoint Properties, plans to sell at least two major residential projects this year.

- Overseas Union Enterprise -- hotel arm of Overseas Union Bank and owner of Mandarin Singapore -- said it is opening US$77 million Hainan Mandarin on August 1, one of first international five-star hotels in Hainan.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore holding roadshows in London, Amsterdam and New York for companies whose shares are in recently-launched Business Times-Singapore Regional Index.
- Ailing modem maker Hayes Microcomputer Products, associate of mainboard-listed Acma Ltd, in merger discussions with U.S.-based Micronics Computers Inc.
- Ossia International, which has been on an aggressive acquisition trail, buys significant stakes in four companies.
